per_question.question: What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?

key_points.key_point: Supervised learning uses labelled input and output pairs
Unsupervised learning works on unlabelled data
Supervised learning predicts a target; unsupervised learning finds structure such as clusters
Classification and regression are supervised; clustering and dimensionality reduction are unsupervised

per_question.question: What caused the 2008 global financial crisis?

key_points.key_point: A US housing bubble and its collapse
Subprime mortgage lending to borrowers who could not repay
Securitisation into mortgage-backed securities and CDOs that obscured risk
Credit rating agencies rated these securities too favourably
High leverage at banks turned losses into insolvency and a credit freeze

per_question.question: How does HTTP/3 differ from HTTP/2?

key_points.key_point: HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP; HTTP/2 uses TCP
Eliminates TCP head-of-line blocking between streams
Faster connection establishment because TLS is integrated into the handshake
Supports connection migration when the network path changes

per_question.question: What is the Paris Agreement and what are its main goals?

key_points.key_point: Adopted in 2015 under the UNFCCC
Goal of limiting warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius, pursuing 1.5 degrees
Countries set their own nationally determined contributions
Contributions are meant to ratchet up over time
Includes transparency and reporting requirements

per_question.question: How do mRNA vaccines work?

key_points.key_point: Delivers mRNA encoding a pathogen protein, often the spike protein
Lipid nanoparticles protect the mRNA and help it enter cells
Host cell ribosomes translate the mRNA into the protein
The immune system responds to that protein, creating antibodies and memory
The mRNA degrades quickly and does not alter host DNA

per_question.question: What is CRISPR-Cas9 and what is it used for?

key_points.key_point: Derived from a bacterial adaptive immune system
A guide RNA targets a specific DNA sequence
The Cas9 enzyme cuts the DNA at that site
Cell repair pathways then disable a gene or insert a new sequence
Applications include research knockouts, gene therapy, and crop engineering

per_question.question: What are the main provisions of the EU General Data Protection Regulation?

key_points.key_point: Took effect in May 2018 and applies to personal data of people in the EU
Requires a lawful basis for processing such as consent
Principles of data minimisation and purpose limitation
Individual rights including access, erasure, rectification, and portability
Breach notification within 72 hours
Fines up to 4 percent of global annual turnover or 20 million euros

per_question.question: What is the transformer architecture in machine learning and why was it significant?

key_points.key_point: Introduced in the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need
Uses self-attention instead of recurrence
Multi-head attention and positional encodings are core components
Parallelises training across sequence positions, unlike RNNs
Handles long-range dependencies well and underpins modern large language models

per_question.question: What is quantum entanglement?

key_points.key_point: Particles share a joint quantum state and cannot be described independently
Measurement outcomes are correlated regardless of separation
Correlations exceed what classical local theories allow, confirmed by Bell tests
Does not permit faster-than-light communication
Relevant to quantum computing and quantum cryptography

Heavy military spending and reliance on oil revenues that declined
Gorbachev's perestroika and glasnost reforms weakened central control
Nationalist and independence movements in the constituent republics
The failed August 1991 coup attempt
Formal dissolution in December 1991

per_question.question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?

key_points.key_point: TCP is connection-oriented; UDP is connectionless
TCP guarantees delivery through acknowledgements and retransmission
TCP preserves ordering; UDP does not
TCP provides flow and congestion control
UDP has lower overhead and latency
TCP suits web and file transfer; UDP suits streaming, voice, and DNS

per_question.question: What is inflation and what are its main causes?

key_points.key_point: A sustained increase in the general price level
Reduces the purchasing power of money
Demand-pull inflation from demand exceeding supply capacity
Cost-push inflation from higher input costs or supply shocks
Excessive money supply growth relative to output
Inflation expectations becoming self-reinforcing

per_question.question: How does solar photovoltaic technology convert sunlight into electricity?

key_points.key_point: Uses semiconductor material, typically silicon
A p-n junction creates an internal electric field
Photons excite electrons into a conducting state, the photovoltaic effect
The junction's field separates charges to produce direct current
An inverter converts DC to AC for grid use

per_question.question: What is the James Webb Space Telescope designed to study?

key_points.key_point: Launched in December 2021
Observes primarily in the infrared
Operates near the Sun-Earth L2 point
Studies the earliest galaxies and highly redshifted light
Studies star and planet formation within dust clouds
Characterises exoplanet atmospheres
Has a segmented primary mirror about 6.5 metres across

per_question.question: What are the health effects of long-term sleep deprivation?

key_points.key_point: Impaired attention, memory, and reaction time
Increased risk of cardiovascular disease and high blood pressure
Impaired glucose metabolism and higher type 2 diabetes risk
Weight gain and appetite hormone disruption
Weakened immune function
Higher risk of depression and anxiety

per_question.question: What is Kubernetes and what problem does it solve?

key_points.key_point: An open source container orchestration system, originating at Google
Schedules containers across a cluster of machines
Self-healing: restarts or replaces failed containers
Horizontal scaling of replicas
Service discovery and load balancing
Rolling updates and rollbacks
Declarative desired-state model reconciled by a control plane

per_question.question: What is the difference between overfitting and underfitting in machine learning?

key_points.key_point: Overfitting: good training performance, poor generalisation to unseen data
Overfitting means the model has learned noise in the training set
Underfitting: poor performance on both training and test data
Underfitting means the model is too simple for the underlying structure
Overfitting is high variance; underfitting is high bias
Remedies include regularisation, more data, or changing model complexity

per_question.question: What is the role of the Federal Reserve in the US economy?

key_points.key_point: The central bank of the United States
Dual mandate of maximum employment and price stability
Sets the federal funds rate target
Uses open market operations to implement policy
Supervises and regulates banks
Acts as lender of last resort in a crisis
Supports the payment and clearing system

per_question.question: How do plants turn sunlight into food?

key_points.key_point: Light energy is captured by the green pigment in leaf cells
Gas taken from the air and water drawn up by the roots are the raw materials
The captured energy is used to build simple sugars the plant lives on
Oxygen leaves the plant as a leftover of the process

per_question.question: Why does vaccinating most of a population also protect the people who are not vaccinated?

key_points.key_point: An infection that cannot find a susceptible host stops spreading
The share of a population that must be immune rises with how easily the disease passes between people
People who cannot be vaccinated are shielded indirectly by those around them
Protection is a property of the group rather than of any one person

per_question.question: Why do central banks raise interest rates when prices are rising quickly?

key_points.key_point: Dearer credit discourages households from spending and firms from investing
Slower demand takes the pressure off prices
The effect arrives long after the decision, so policy is set on forecasts
Overdoing it costs output and jobs

per_question.question: What happens between typing a web address and the page appearing?

key_points.key_point: The name is first turned into a numeric address
That lookup is answered from a saved copy where one exists, rather than repeated every time
The browser then opens a connection and asks for the document
The document points at further files that are fetched before the page is drawn

per_question.question: Why do antibiotics stop working over time?

key_points.key_point: Survivors of treatment are the ones that reproduce, so the survivable trait becomes common
Bacteria also hand these traits to other bacteria directly
Every course given when it was not needed adds to the pressure
Replacement drugs arrive more slowly than the problem spreads

per_question.question: Why do earthquakes happen where they do?

key_points.key_point: The planet's outer shell is broken into slabs that move against each other
Most shaking happens along the lines where two slabs meet
Friction holds the rock until accumulated strain releases in a sudden slip
A few happen far from any boundary, along old lines of weakness

per_question.question: Why does saving early matter more than saving more later?

key_points.key_point: Each period's gain joins the sum that earns the next one
The balance grows by multiplication rather than by addition, so the curve steepens
Money put in decades earlier passes through far more periods of growth
A charge taken yearly also removes everything that money would have gone on to earn

per_question.question: Why does adding certain gases to the atmosphere warm the planet?

key_points.key_point: Incoming light passes through the air and heats the ground
The warmed ground sends energy back out at longer wavelengths
Certain gases soak up part of that outgoing energy and send some of it back down
The surface must therefore get warmer before what leaves matches what arrives
A warmer atmosphere holds more water vapour, which does the same thing and enlarges the effect

per_question.question: How can two computers agree on a secret key while someone is listening to everything they send?

key_points.key_point: Each side keeps one value to itself and sends a value derived from it
Both can reach the same answer from what they kept and what they received
An eavesdropper who saw only what was sent cannot work the answer out in any usable time
A signed credential shows the other side is who it claims, not an impostor relaying messages
The agreed value is then used with a faster method for the bulk of the traffic

per_question.question: Why does the sea rise and fall roughly twice a day?

key_points.key_point: The Moon pulls harder on the near side of the Earth than on the far side
It is that difference across the planet, not the strength of the pull, that raises the water
The oceans are stretched into two bulges, one facing the Moon and one opposite it
A coastline turns through both bulges in about a day, so there are two high waters
The Sun adds to the effect when it lines up with the Moon and works against it at right angles
